column1: # The release's pins (TVI-WO-1200), tab-separated, one home for each. Read by tools/tviburi-release, which
# names every row in the MANIFEST it writes.
#   build  <assembly> <build string> <sha256>   the consumer's pinned Renode (RUL-09), read from the image's assemblies
#                                      (TVI-WO-0100b FEEDBACK §2 item 5): `renode` is Renode.dll, `infrastructure` is
#                                      Infrastructure.dll, each under the Renode root. Tviburi's runner checks the first's
#                                      string against `renode --version`. The release refuses to build unless each
#                                      assembly's sha256 is the one named here, so a release names only the assemblies it
#                                      was built against (TVI-WO-2100 Q25). The sha256 is there because the string alone
#                                      cannot name the rebuilt Infrastructure.dll (AET-WO-1605): it reports the unpatched
#                                      string, 1.0.0+cd4b002a..., because the rebuild sets SourceRevisionId to that same
#                                      commit, so only its hash tells it from Antmicro's build. The MANIFEST's `build` lines
#                                      carry both, string and sha256.
#   stock  <sha256> <path>             the stm32h753.repl include chain, in include order, as Aethelgard pins it
#                                      (crates/aethelgard-twin/src/platform.rs RENODE_FILES); read under Renode's root
#   class  <stock type> <guard type> <stock instances> <consumer instances>   the class map (RUL-09): one row per
#                                      guard, never two. Both columns are required (TVI-WO-1203), names one space apart,
#                                      `-` for none, no name twice. A stock instance must be one the pinned chain declares
#                                      with that type; it is `restate`d in the MANIFEST, and the release refuses it unless
#                                      a committed model/stm32h7-*-restate.repl declares it under the guard and the
#                                      committed replay (tests/1301/replay-1301.sh) loads that file. A consumer instance
#                                      must be one the chain does not declare; it is `retype`d, and the release refuses
#                                      it unless the consumer's committed platform (the ArduPilot fixture under
#                                      tests/1301/fixtures/) declares it with the stock type and one of the replay's
#                                      re-typing rules turns it into the guard, names compared case-sensitively (SPI's
#                                      spi1, spi2). Planted and refused by tests/spike.sh manifest
